raw_response:
**My thinking as this farmer:**

I've been working this land for 35 years. I know Quzhou's soil — it's alkaline, sandy in places, and the summers get dry fast if you're not watching the well. My main income comes from cotton. That's always been the center of my system. Wheat and maize feed the family and whatever's left over sells at the township market. The stevia is a small patch I keep because the purchase station buys it and it brings in extra cash without much extra work.

My land is 22.1 mu. I'll put 10 mu in cotton — that's my main crop, always has been. The other 12 mu I double-crop: winter wheat planted in October, then summer maize straight after the wheat harvest in June. No need to till between them, I just direct-seed the maize. That saves me time and my sons aren't always home to help. A small strip — about 0.1 mu near the house — I keep for stevia.

For cotton, I use the improved varieties from the seed station. Hybrids cost too much and I don't always trust the yield claims. Six pesticide rounds are normal for cotton here — bollworm and aphid pressure is real every year. I irrigate four times from the well: before planting, at bud stage, flowering, and boll expansion. For wheat, I plough in October before sowing — maize stubble needs to go under properly. Three irrigations: one in winter to protect against freeze damage, one at jointing, one at heading. For maize, I skip tilling entirely and sow directly. Two irrigations are usually enough since we get summer rain, but I'm ready for a third if July is dry.

The stevia plot I hand-tend myself. It needs more water per mu than anything else but it's a tiny area so it's fine.
